subject: the lane type File > Import > MIDI File creates, and copying its region onto a Software Instrument track
question: record_sequence always ends in State B imported_as_gm_device on this host. Does a GM program change in the file, or a selected Software Instrument track, change the lane Logic creates? If not, can the region be moved onto an audible track and verified?

reverify.command: In a project whose track 0 is a Software Instrument track, call logic_tracks record_sequence {bar: 3, notes: "67,0,500,100;69,600,500,100", target_track: 0, target_expected_name: <track 0 name>}; then repeat with a wrong target_expected_name.
reverify.expected: The first answers State A with verify_source ax_region_delta, recorded_to_track 0 and gm_device_lane_retained true; the second refuses at relocation_preflight with write_attempted false and no new lane.

method: A control import (the server's own SMF, notes only) and a test import (a hand-written format 0 SMF with the same notes plus Program Change 0 on channel 1) were made through the same menu path with a Software Instrument track selected, declining the tempo prompt as the server does. Lane names were read with logic_project inspect_session. The move was first done by hand with tracks.select, edit.cut, tracks.select, transport.goto_position and edit.paste, read back with project.get_regions, and confirmed by ear; the implemented relocation uses copy instead of cut.

observations.probe: import of the server's notes-only SMF with track 0 (a Software Instrument) selected
import of the same notes plus Program Change 0 on channel 1
observations.note: a GM program does not make Logic pick a software instrument on this host

observations.probe: select the new lane, cut, select track 0, playhead at bar 1, paste
observations.regions_after: the region on track 0, bars 1-2; the source lane empty
observations.audible: yes, confirmed by ear through track 0's instrument

observations.operation: record_sequence with target_track 0 and a wrong target_expected_name
record_sequence bar 3 with target_track 0 and the correct name

conclusion: On this host MIDI file import always creates a new External MIDI lane, whatever the file's program change or the current selection, so the notes-only fix is not available in the file. Selecting a track selects its regions, so copy from the new lane and paste onto a named Software Instrument track at bar 1 moves the take with its bar offset intact, and a new region on the target at the imported bars is independent evidence the move happened.
limits: Single-channel sequences only: a multichannel SMF creates several lanes and is refused rather than guessed at.
The GM lane is retained, not deleted; removing it stays an explicit, name-corroborated tracks.delete.
If the target already holds a region with the same name and bars, the paste cannot be told apart from it and the call fails closed as paste_unverified.
Other Logic versions may create Software Instrument lanes directly (the README demo implies 12.3 did on its host); there the relocation path is simply never taken.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record states a fact about Logic's BEHAVIOUR -- when the MIDI file Open panel accepts a key, where its buttons sit in the AX tree, what kind of lane an import creates -- not about a string Logic ships. There is no key to cite and nothing to prove absent. Rule 13 checks the claim: if any reading here resolved in the corpus the declaration would be refused.
